stem.text: Evaluate the improper integral \( \int_{3}^{6} \frac{3 x^{2}}{\sqrt{x^{3} - 27}}\,dx \), or show that it diverges.

worked_solution.text: The integral is improper because the integrand is unbounded as x approaches 3 from the right, so write it as \( \lim_{R\to 3^{+}} \int_{R}^{6} \frac{3 x^{2}}{\sqrt{x^{3} - 27}}\,dx \).
Substitute \( u = x^{3} - 27,\ du = 3 x^{2}\,dx \). The limits become \( u = R^{3} - 27 \text{ to } u = 189 \), and an antiderivative in u is \( 2 \sqrt{u} \).
Evaluate the limit: \( \lim_{R\to 3^{+}} \left( 6 \sqrt{21} - 2\sqrt{R^{3} - 27} \right) = 6 \sqrt{21} \). The limit is finite, so the integral converges to \( 6 \sqrt{21} \).

options.label: The integral converges to \( 18 \sqrt{21} \).
options.derivation: the factor 1/3 that du introduces dropped

options.label: The integral converges to \( - 2 \sqrt{3} + 2 \sqrt{6} \).

options.label: The integral converges to \( - 6 \sqrt{3} + 6 \sqrt{6} \).
